components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Outline Button

components.name: Verification Seal
components.description: The signature mark: a brass wax-seal disc that means evaluated and approved.
components.css: .ds-seal { width: 3rem; height: 3rem; border-radius: 50%; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #fff; background: radial-gradient(circle at 32% 26%, #e0b563, #a9761f 62%, #8c6017); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px rgba(255,255,255,0.4), inset 0 0 0 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.06), 0 3px 8px rgba(140,96,23,0.35); }

components.name: Subject Badge
components.description: Default categorizer for asignaturas; pine tint.
components.css: .ds-badge-subject { display: inline-block; font-family: 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.8rem; color: #1a4d3a; background: #e7efe9; border: 1px solid #d8e6dc; border-radius: 0.4rem; padding: 0.34em 0.6em; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Directory filter field; pine focus ring.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Buscar por nombre o asignatura">
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; color: #17241e; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #d3d7cc; border-radius: 0.55rem; padding: 0.55rem 0.8rem; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #78877d; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #1f5c46; box-shadow: 0 0 0 0.2rem rgba(31,92,70,0.15); }

components.name: Directory Card
components.description: A teacher's registry entry: dossier card, flat at rest, lifts on hover.

narrative.overview: Reemplazos de Profes looks and behaves like an official register of vetted professionals, because that is exactly what it sells: a database of substitute teachers each screened by a sicóloga laboral before they appear. The interface carries the quiet authority of a credentialing body — deep evergreen, a warm brass reserved almost exclusively for the verification seal, and a cool paper ground that feels like a well-kept record. The system is refined and institutional: brand personality lives in small exact details, not loud gradients. Trust is the product, so the design states, certifies, and gets out of the way. The rejected world is the generic SaaS starter — indigo-to-violet hero gradients, Inter as the default, one rounded-card shadow on everything, emoji section markers.
keyCharacteristics: Evergreen + brass on cool paper — an academic credential palette, never the default blue.
A recurring brass verification seal as the system's signature mark.
Serif headlines (Spectral) for authority; Public Sans for trust; IBM Plex Mono for data/record text.
Flat, hairline-bordered surfaces that lift only on interaction.
Spanish-Chilean vernacular treated as content, not decoration.

rules.name: The Scarce Brass Rule
rules.body: Brass is ceremonial, not structural. It appears only where the product certifies something — the seal, a rating, a mono eyebrow, or the one primary nav CTA — never as a general-purpose button or background.

rules.name: The No-Blue Rule
rules.body: There is no blue in this system. The instinct to reach for a trustworthy SaaS blue is exactly the generic default this identity rejects; trust is carried by evergreen and the seal.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Record Rule
rules.body: Monospace is never decorative. It marks text that is a datum or a category label — a result count, a rating, PASO 01, SELLO DE EVALUACIÓN. If it isn't a record, it isn't mono.

rules.name: The Serif-Authority Rule
rules.body: Headings and proper names of people/schools are set in Spectral; UI chrome and controls are Public Sans. Never set a button or form label in the serif.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: If a surface isn't being interacted with, it carries at most the hairline shadow. Let the border do the separating.

dos: Do keep brass ceremonial — seal, ratings, mono eyebrows, one nav CTA.
Do set headings and proper names in Spectral, and all UI chrome in Public Sans.
Do use IBM Plex Mono only for data/record text (counts, ratings, PASO 01, eyebrows).
Do keep surfaces flat at rest and reserve real elevation for hover, the hero, and the floating sample card.
Do encode state in color and label together (verified/pending/rejected pills).
Do speak the real vernacular — comuna, RBD, asignatura, reemplazo corto/largo — as visible content.
donts: Don't introduce blue, or an indigo→violet gradient — the No-Blue Rule is absolute.
Don't stamp a drop shadow on every card; let the hairline border separate resting surfaces.
Don't spend brass as a general button or background color.
Don't use the verification seal on anything that isn't an approved profile.
Don't set body copy or controls in the serif, or a data label in the body sans.
Don't center everything or reach for emoji as section markers; structure should encode real meaning.
